assumptions: vocab_added being empty is read as 'no new slot values were minted this run' — the full 5070-hypothesis population was built by recombining an already-fixed action/mechanism/actor/place/period vocabulary, not by discovering new categories.

The reported missing_mass (0.0418) is treated as a Good-Turing-style per-draw unseen-probability estimate, not as '1 minus fraction of species observed'. This is assumed because it is inconsistent with the chao1_estimate: observed/chao1 = 5070/33686 ≈ 0.15, implying ~85% of estimated distinct hypothesis-types are still unobserved, which is a very different (much larger) number than 4.2%. Both can be true simultaneously only under a long-tail distribution where most unseen types are individually low-probability — this is model-prior reasoning about Good-Turing estimators, not something stated in the run data, so it is flagged as low-confidence interpretation rather than fact.

coverage_low/coverage_high (0.089-0.491) are assumed to bound the *coverage fraction* (share of true diversity observed), which independently corroborates that a large, uncertain chunk of the hypothesis space (roughly 51%-91% missing) is unrepresented, even though the point missing_mass statistic looks small.

robustness_stable_fraction (0.9815) is read as a structural-stability signal (survivors are insensitive to perturbation), separate from and not sufficient to offset the calibration_brier (0.353) evidence of poor score accuracy — the meta_review's 'templated opinion floats' finding is taken as the likely mechanical cause of that poor calibration.

target_blind.first_run=True and prior_rate=None are taken to mean there is literally no prior-run baseline; the pipeline's 'steady': True flag is therefore treated as a default/placeholder rather than a computed verified comparison, per instructions not to present unverified pipeline output as established fact.
incomplete_vocabularies: Action slot: borrows-from, shares-etymology-with, structurally-echoes, precedes-chronologically, derives-from-common-source, common-source-reconstruction, other-action — generated across many hypotheses but essentially all instances sit frozen at u=1.0 (uninformative prior, b=0/d=0), meaning no evidence has actually been brought to bear to discriminate these values.
Mechanism slot: independent-invention, human-scholarly-comparison — same frozen-at-prior pattern as above; nominally present in the vocabulary but never adjudicated against evidence.

Actor slot (skeptical/debunking readings): mythicist-non-historicity, euhemerist-deification, channeled-modern-revelation — each appears as a single isolated hypothesis with near-zero apriori weight (~0.018-0.047) and is frozen at u=1.0; too thin (n=1 each) to say anything about how the generator treats this class.

Place slot as applied to 'confucius'-as-object hypotheses — defaults to 'hinduism' regardless of actor/tradition, which the meta-review flags as a likely generation bug; treated here as incomplete/unreliable coverage rather than genuine evidentiary thinness, since it may be inflating combinatorial count without adding real place-vocabulary signal.

Period/interval slot for the span -500 to 1863 — collapsed into a single undifferentiated catch-all bucket [-500,1863] reused for Buddha/Confucius/Bahaullah/Jesus/Laozi cross-era claims, with no Hellenistic/Roman/Late-Antique/Medieval/Early-Modern subdivisions ever tested; this is a coarse, evidentially thin temporal vocabulary relative to the fine-grained axial-age (-1500..-500) subdivisions.
calibration_summary: This run shows a generator that is structurally stable (98.15% of survivors robust to perturbation) but evaluatively shallow: it added zero new vocabulary, spent most of its 5070-hypothesis budget on combinatorial padding (actor/place permutations around a handful of hub objects) rather than genuinely new content, and the meta-review's evidence of verbatim-repeated opinion floats across unrelated actor/object pairs points to scoring-by-template (action×mechanism) rather than per-hypothesis evaluation — a plausible mechanical driver of the middling-to-poor Brier score (0.353) despite a moderate surprise rate (0.214). The richness estimate (chao1 ≈ 33,686 against 5070 observed, with a wide coverage interval of ~0.09-0.49) suggests a substantial long tail of hypothesis-types remains unexplored even though the point missing-mass statistic is small, and several action/mechanism/actor slot-values are present nominally but never actually adjudicated (frozen at the uninformative prior), meaning apparent vocabulary breadth overstates real evidentiary coverage. Overall: treat this run's coverage and calibration numbers as indicating a generator that is diverse in label surface but narrow in genuine discrimination, with real risk that reported confidence (low Brier-implied precision) is inflated by templated scoring rather than earned by case-specific evidence.
target_blind_note: The run record marks target_blind.steady=True, but target_blind.first_run=True and prior_rate=None — there is no actual prior-run proposal rate to compare against, so 'steady' cannot have been computed as a real comparison; it reads as a default placeholder for a first run rather than a verified finding. Per the instruction to read a falling non-consensus proposal rate the same way as a falling surprise rate (a target-blindness health signal), we have no baseline here to detect a fall against, so this check is inconclusive rather than confirmed-healthy. This should be treated as model-prior-adjacent caution, not as an established 'steady' result: the next run, once it has a real prior_rate to compare its 0.15 non-consensus proposal rate against, will be the first point where this signal is actually testable.
